question.text: An SIA report intended for retail donors should prioritise which of the following combinations per Chapter 7.3.2 principles?

answer.text: Transparency and materiality while being as short as possible to hold stakeholders' attention
Length over brevity — the longer the better
Highly technical SROI tables with no narrative

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7.3.2: 'The report should also be as short as possible while meeting principles of transparency and materiality which stakeholders should be interested in reading and should get quick required information.' Brevity + material substance is the target. The Trap: A wrongly equates length with rigour. C is inaccessible to retail. D sacrifices substance for form. Cross-Exam Context: Retail-friendly disclosure mirrors V-A MF Distributor KIM/SID principles — short, material, readable. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Target a 12-16 page SIR for retail-facing donors, with a one-page executive summary and a two-page infographic. Detail tables should live in annexures. This mirrors the 'inverted pyramid' style used in annual-report highlights sections.
